ruled: EDGE-DEFINITIONS ITEM 9 IS TAKEN: FOUR EDGES THE OUTSIDE WORLD HAS AND APOLLO LACKS. Dave's answer, pasted in chat #308 at 09:26 BST, verbatim: '9. Four edges the outside world has and Apollo lacks — Take it' (the page's recommendation; he took all nine). He answered v1 of the research page (his copy header reads 'Session 308 · edge definitions · answers', without v2's '(v2)', and item 9 reads 'Four edges', v1's wording), so the item is quoted from v1 as written, verbatim: 'Each is a separate yes or no. You can take this item whole or say which letters you want. a) Token → token alias, with a loop check. The design-token standard says circular references must be detected, and Apollo’s token tiers imply alias chains it does not draw. b) Provides capability, the other half of acceptsCapability. The verbs file notes that “no providesCapability is minted”, and Backstage always pairs provides with consumes. c) Something for “default for a theme” to point at: either a theme node kind or the theme as a qualifier on the edge. Today both defaults are declared nulls. d) Component → ARIA role. ARIA’s own required-context and required-owned rules could then be checked against containedBy and hasPart. Why: each one closes a gap that a named standard already covers. None of them is invented here.' v2's change, not ruled; his: v2 adds a fifth edge, verbatim: 'e) Replaced-by on components and tokens, with the version it happened in. Spectrum carries introduced, deprecatedIn, replacedBy and plannedRemoval on every entity, and the design-token format has $deprecated. Apollo has replacement only between rulings.' Also v2's lean on (c), not ruled; his: 'c) A theme node kind, so “default for a theme” has something to point at. v2 leans to a node: Canonical models themes and modes as coordinates with a fallback, and Tokens Studio as theme groups and options. Today both defaults are declared nulls.' He answered v1: four edges, and (c) is left as either a theme node kind or the theme as a qualifier on the edge.
